messages:
Aditya Rao: collecting beta cohort feedback (SE + Support) on tiered batching defaults before we lock GA scope. pls drop: what’s working, what’s confusing, what’s breaking + proposed fixes. Also: anything we need to change in docs/console.

Miguel Santos: from SE calls this week (VertexWave + 2 smaller startups):
- biggest ask: “show me what’s actually running.” they keep asking for effective config (tier + computed knobs) per route/model. Console dropdown alone isn’t enough.
- cost-efficient tier perceived as “riskier” unless we can point to clear guardrails + rollback behavior.
- they want to set tier per route (chat vs embeddings) + override one knob (queue delay) without “falling off the supported path.”
- wording: cost-efficient is fine; “eco” was confusing. also people interpret “standard” as “current default” (which it isn’t yet).

Soojin Lee: +1 on naming. On the messaging side, “cost-efficient” is clear, “fast” is clear. For “standard,” we should explicitly describe it as balanced, not necessarily “default,” until we actually default it.
Also: in the FAQ we should explicitly say “tiers change batching + scheduling; output quality should be unchanged, but sampling variance can show up.” We’ve had 2 prospects ask “does batching change the model?”

Monica Patel: support is seeing confusion around tier vs explicit batching overrides. SUP-18510 basically: customer set `batching_tier=cost_efficient` and also has legacy `max_batch=8` in their config, then expects the tier to win. They’re upset when nothing changes.
We need docs and/or API error/warn: “explicit batching config overrides tier defaults.”
Maybe in response headers we include something like:
- `x-redwood-batching-tier-effective: cost_efficient`
- `x-redwood-batching-overrides-effective: max_batch,max_queue_delay_ms`
Even if Console shows it, they want it in logs.

Alex Martinez: from DevEx side: can we make the “override” story less sharp? Right now it’s all-or-nothing in people’s heads.
Suggestion: docs pattern:
1) set tier
2) optionally override a single knob w/ a clear warning that you’re diverging from Redwood-recommended profile
3) point to troubleshoot section for tail latency + timeouts
If we ship that plus a “reset to recommended” button in Console, SEs will be happier.

Rafael Mendes: from on-call during beta ramp: the customers who got into trouble were mostly high concurrency + tight timeouts + cost-efficient tier. queue delay + overload protection interactions were the culprit.
Support escalations mention “timeouts went up” not “latency went up.” We should be explicit in docs: if your client timeout < p95 target you will see failures.
Also: for GA we need a single page that says “if cost-efficient increases timeouts, do A/B to standard, and watch X metrics.” (INT-3301 is asking for a playbook.)

Aisha Bello: observability feedback (from SEs trying to validate): they want a small “what to watch” checklist. Right now dashboards are too many.
Minimum set they keep asking for:
- p95 end-to-end latency (by route/model/tier)
- queue delay p95
- batch size distribution
- timeout/cancel rate
- GPU util
If we can embed that as a Console link next to tier selection (“View tier health dashboard”), would reduce confusion.

Marissa Cole: rollout/product note: multiple folks asked “what happens if it’s bad?” We should document the auto-rollback signals in plain language (e.g., timeout rate + p99 regression thresholds) and that we can pause ramps.
Also: opt-out mechanism needs to be obvious. Some customers don’t want any automated changes; they want a pinned tier per route.

Wei Chen: docs delta list from support/SE comments:
- add a table: Tier -> intent -> tradeoffs -> “don’t use if…”
- explicitly state precedence: explicit batching knobs > tier defaults > platform defaults
- add a troubleshooting section referencing common failure modes:
  - streaming cadence complaints (fast tier) => recommend fast tier only for streaming + watch token cadence metrics
  - timeouts (cost-efficient) => reduce client timeout sensitivity, switch to standard, or cap max_queue_delay
  - long-context spikes => mention model-family overrides may differ
I can update docs PR but need final language from product.

Aditya Rao: super helpful. summarizing proposed changes before GA:
1) Make “effective config” visible (Console + response headers) incl. which fields are overridden.
2) Docs: precedence rules + “don’t use if…” + minimal dashboard checklist + troubleshooting playbook.
3) Messaging: don’t imply “standard” == default until we flip it; keep “cost-efficient” name.
4) Rollout story: document auto-rollback + obvious opt-out/pinning per route.

Aditya Rao: open questions to resolve this week:
- do we want headers by default for hosted? (or only when `debug=true` / console toggle)
- do we add a config validation warning when both tier + explicit knobs set?
- should “standard” become default for a subset of models/regions at GA or stay opt-in?

Miguel Santos: re headers: SEs love it for proof during pilots. even a single header “effective tier + profile version” would help.
Maybe:
- `x-redwood-batching-profile: standard@v1`
- `x-redwood-batching-overrides: none` (or list)

Monica Patel: validation warning would cut ticket volume a lot. even just returning a 200 w/ warning in response metadata would help (we can’t break people).
Also: we need a canned response snippet for support:
“Tier changes defaults only; if you’ve set `max_batch/max_queue_delay` explicitly, tier won’t change behavior.”

Rafael Mendes: +1 to warning. For defaulting standard: I’d rather we keep it opt-in until we’ve got stable dashboards + rollback hooks everywhere. we had that brief latency spike when ramping (we paused fast).
If we do default anything, do it only in 1 region + 1-2 models w/ conservative guardrails.

Soojin Lee: agree. we can market “standard is recommended starting point” without claiming it’s the platform default.
Also we should avoid too many new terms. “profile version” is good but keep it simple in customer-facing copy.

Aisha Bello: if we add headers, please keep names stable; dashboards can correlate by tier label already. If we add “profile version,” we should also label it in metrics so it’s searchable.

Aditya Rao: ok. action items I’ll drive:
- align w/ platform team on effective-config endpoint/headers (ties to Console explainability).
- update GA checklist: docs + playbook + warning + minimal dashboards link.
- decide defaulting strategy w/ SRE (likely opt-in at GA, staged default later).

Aditya Rao: if you have any more cohort-specific notes (LuminaAI, etc.) drop them here by EOD tomorrow so we can incorporate into release notes + final FAQ.
